claims.claim: On September 28, 2026, NVIDIA launched the Open Agent Safety Platform, combining software sandboxing with hardware-level DPU monitoring to contain autonomous AI agents.
The platform introduces OpenShell, an open-source sealed runtime environment that sandboxes agent workspaces and enforces operational security boundaries.
claims.notes: Open-source software layer compatible across compute platforms.

claims.claim: The Sentry hardware monitoring system operates out-of-band on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs, capable of quarantining rogue agents within milliseconds independent of the host CPU/GPU.
claims.notes: Out-of-band monitoring ensures agents cannot disable their own supervisors.

claims.claim: The platform is backed by Microsoft, Anthropic, Cisco, SAP, JPMorganChase, and SpaceX.
claims.notes: Broad coalition; OpenAI not part of the initial launch group.

claims.claim: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang characterized AI safety as an engineering and datacenter infrastructure challenge solved through automated containment rather than halting progress.
claims.notes: Focuses on architectural isolation and DPU-enforced firewalls.

editorial_cautions: Distinguish between OpenShell (software sandbox) and Sentry (hardware DPU out-of-band monitoring).
Highlight that out-of-band DPU execution prevents rogue agents from tampering with the supervisor.
